confirmation-statement.title: When do you need to file?

items.title: Every year
items.text: Most UK limited companies must file a Confirmation Statement at least once every 12 months, even if the company is dormant or no details have changed.

items.title: 14-day filing deadline
items.text: You generally have 14 days after the end of your review period to file your Confirmation Statement with Companies House.

items.title: Keep your company details up to date
items.text: If certain details change during the year, you may need to notify Companies House separately rather than waiting until your next Confirmation Statement.

dormant-company-accounts.title: What a dormant company still needs to do

items.title: Annual accounts
items.text: Dormant accounts must still be prepared and filed with Companies House each year.

items.title: Confirmation Statement
items.text: A Confirmation Statement is still due at least once every 12 months.

items.title: Tell HMRC where needed
items.text: You may need to tell HMRC the company is dormant for Corporation Tax.

self-assessment-tax-return.title: Who needs to file a Self Assessment tax return?
self-assessment-tax-return.intro: You may need to submit a Self Assessment tax return if you:
items: A sole trader or individual whose gross self-employment income exceeds £1,000 in a tax year, before expenses, or a business partner.
Earn income from letting property or land.
Receive income from construction work as a self-employed subcontractor.
Your income is above the level where HMRC requires a return.
You or your partner’s adjusted net income exceeds £60,000 and the High Income Child Benefit Charge applies.
Have taxable savings interest, dividends or other investment income.
Receive foreign income that is taxable in the UK.
Need to claim eligible tax reliefs through Self Assessment.
Have taxable gains from selling assets, such as property or shares, that must be reported to HMRC.
HMRC has instructed you to submit a tax return.

cta.title: Not sure whether you need to file?
cta.text: Not everyone in these categories automatically needs to file; it depends on your circumstances and the tax rules. ABF can help you understand your obligations and next steps.
